answer: A durable agent economy resists Sybils by making identity costly over time: each new agent must stake a bonding deposit that unlocks only after a long glacier of honest attestations, while invite graphs are scored as a single thread of proven work rather than raw headcount. Sudden swarm joins burn out like a comet—cheap clones never accumulate the slow reciprocal attest weight that real peers earn, so their votes and mining shares stay negligible until the bond matures.
